policy_name: Guidance for the safe and responsible use of Generative AI in the Victorian Public Sector
issuing_authority: Victorian Government – Department of Government Services (Cyber Security, Data and Digital Resilience Division)
regulatory_regime: Supports the Administrative Guideline for the safe and responsible use of Generative AI in the Victorian Public Sector
geo_constraints: Victorian public sector bodies and public entities (Public Administration Act 2004)

locale_context.regulation: Staff guidance · practical do/don't advice under a state administrative guideline
locale_context.culture: Victorian state public-sector guidance grounded in the Charter of Human Rights, privacy and public-records law: practical, personnel-facing advice that keeps humans accountable and treats Generative AI as one input rather than a decision-maker.

versions.title: Guidance for the safe and responsible use of Generative AI in the Victorian Public Sector
versions.summary: Only one version recorded for this policy.
versions.note: The document prints no date or version number; 2024-11 is the .docx file's created/modified date (15 Nov 2024) and is only an approximation. The text post-dates June 2024 (refers to Victoria agreeing to the National AI Assurance Framework then).

covered_entities: public sector personnel: employees, contractors, consultants and volunteers of public sector bodies and public entities (Public Administration Act 2004)
covered_activities: use of Generative AI tools for official work purposes
entering information into Generative AI tools
using and attributing Generative AI outputs
conditions: may be complemented by organisation- or sector-specific policies
general advice only; not legal advice
objective: Give Victorian public sector personnel practical guidance for safe and responsible use of publicly-available and agency-approved Generative AI tools, supporting the Generative AI Administrative Guideline.
principles: privacy and safeguarding public sector information
parent_policy: Administrative Guideline for the safe and responsible use of Generative AI in the Victorian Public Sector

related_policies.policy: Administrative Guideline for the safe and responsible use of Generative AI in the Victorian Public Sector

conflict_rule: General advice only, not legal advice; personnel must still meet legislative obligations (Privacy and Data Protection Act 2014, Charter of Human Rights and Responsibilities Act 2006, Public Records Act 1973, Public Administration Act 2004) and organisation-specific policies.

record_provenance.notes: Text taken from the copy in asago-ai/asago-policy-mapper (policy_examples/vps.docx). Title from the document heading and footer. clauses.section: When using Generative AI tools – Maintain accountability, transparency and explainability (Do)
clauses.original_text: Remain responsible and accountable for content you create, share or use while performing your official work. Fact-check information against verifiable sources. Attribute any content to the appropriate Generative AI tool.
clauses.requirement: stay accountable for AI-assisted work, fact-check outputs against verifiable sources and attribute content to the Generative AI tool used
clauses.purpose: accuracy and explainability of government work open to merit and judicial review
clauses.affected_asset: integrity of government decisions and records
clauses.applicable_systems: publicly-available and agency-approved Generative AI tools used for official work
clauses.interpretation_notes: Quoted from the 'When using Generative AI tools' Do/Don't tables (pandoc text of the .docx); table cell line breaks collapsed. Same table also asks staff to keep records of inputs and AI-generated content incorporated into official documents.

clauses.section: When using Generative AI tools – Maintain accountability, transparency and explainability (Don’t)
clauses.original_text: Use these tools to make decisions, undertake assessments or use them for other administrative actions that may have consequences for individuals, groups or organisations.
clauses.action: do not use Generative AI to make decisions or assessments
clauses.requirement: do not use Generative AI tools to make decisions or assessments with consequences for individuals, groups or organisations
clauses.purpose: fair, explainable decisions that can be upheld on review
clauses.affected_asset: rights and interests of affected persons
clauses.applicable_systems: publicly-available and agency-approved Generative AI tools used for official work
clauses.interpretation_notes: Quoted from the 'When using Generative AI tools' Do/Don't tables (pandoc text of the .docx); table cell line breaks collapsed. A related Don't under 'Be aware of fairness and human rights' says not to 'Allow Generative AI to make decisions for the Victorian Government.'

clauses.section: When using Generative AI tools – Protect privacy and safeguard public sector information (Do / Don’t)
clauses.original_text: Only use publicly available information with publicly available Generative AI tools. … Input, upload or share any public sector information not available in a publicly available publication into publicly-available Generative AI tools.
clauses.recipient: publicly-available and agency-approved Generative AI tools
clauses.requirement: enter only publicly available information into public Generative AI tools; in agency-approved tools stay within the protective marking and permitted purpose
clauses.condition: publicly-available tools: only already-published information; agency-approved tools: within the tool's protective marking, permitted purpose and privacy/security assessments
clauses.purpose: prevent interference with privacy and data breaches, incl. offshore storage by foreign-owned providers
clauses.applicable_systems: publicly-available and agency-approved Generative AI tools used for official work
clauses.interpretation_notes: Quoted from the 'When using Generative AI tools' Do/Don't tables (pandoc text of the .docx); table cell line breaks collapsed. First sentence is a 'Do', the second a 'Don't' from the same table.

clauses.section: When using Generative AI tools – Be aware of fairness and human rights (Don’t)
clauses.original_text: Assume or trust that outputs generated are unbiased, accurate or understand local context or nuance. Rely on Generative AI as the only input to your work (it is just one input). It should not replace your own research, analysis and content development.
clauses.requirement: treat outputs as potentially biased or inaccurate and never as the sole input to work
clauses.purpose: respect human rights under the Victorian Charter of Human Rights and Responsibilities Act 2006
clauses.applicable_systems: publicly-available and agency-approved Generative AI tools used for official work
clauses.interpretation_notes: Quoted from the 'When using Generative AI tools' Do/Don't tables (pandoc text of the .docx); table cell line breaks collapsed.

clauses.section: When using Generative AI tools – Consider reliability and safety (Don’t)
clauses.original_text: Attempt to bypass a Generative AI’s built-in safety measures and ethical restrictions (jailbreaking) to produce an inappropriate response.
clauses.object: Generative AI safety measures and ethical restrictions
clauses.requirement: do not bypass built-in safety measures of Generative AI tools
clauses.purpose: safe use; prevent harmful or deceptive outputs
clauses.affected_asset: Generative AI tool safeguards; the public
clauses.applicable_systems: publicly-available and agency-approved Generative AI tools used for official work
clauses.interpretation_notes: Quoted from the 'When using Generative AI tools' Do/Don't tables (pandoc text of the .docx); table cell line breaks collapsed. The same table recommends agency-approved tools ahead of publicly-available ones.

clauses.section: When using Generative AI tools – Consider legal obligations (Do / Don’t)
clauses.original_text: When generating images, videos, or voice content, ensure that the solution provider provides legal coverage, including fair treatment of artists and respect for intellectual property rights. … Enter any information that may breach another person’s intellectual property rights or legal professional privilege.
clauses.action: ensure IP coverage; do not enter protected information
clauses.object: IP-protected or privileged information; generated images, video and voice
clauses.requirement: do not input material that may breach IP or legal professional privilege; ensure providers give legal coverage for generated media
clauses.condition: image, video or voice generation (first sentence)
clauses.purpose: comply with IP, contractual and privilege obligations
clauses.applicable_systems: publicly-available and agency-approved Generative AI tools used for official work
clauses.interpretation_notes: Quoted from the 'When using Generative AI tools' Do/Don't tables (pandoc text of the .docx); table cell line breaks collapsed. First sentence is a 'Do', the second a 'Don't' from the same table.
